name: splitscreenme-vscode
description: IntelliSense, docs, linting and packaging for Nucleus Co-op game handlers (SplitScreen.Me).

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In a folder you don't trust yet, the checks, completion, docs, Format and Try it work. Install, Test in Nucleus Co-op and Set up AI agents ask you to trust the folder first, and a folder's own game folder links (splitscreenme.gameFolders) are ignored.

semanticTokenModifiers.description: A Nucleus object that holds options, or an enum (Game.ProtoInput, Game.Hook, Nucleus.Folder)
One of a Nucleus enum's fixed values (Nucleus.Folder.InstancedGameFolder)

commands.title: Try It: Test All Combinations (Players, Input, Monitors)
Fix All Problems That Can Be Fixed
Set Up AI Agent Support (AGENTS.md, skill, CLI)
Check All Handlers in the Workspace
Try It: Nucleus Did Something Different…

enumDescriptions: JavaScript files that assign Game.GUID/GameName/ExecutableName/Play/…, or live in a "handlers" folder.
Treat every JavaScript file as a Nucleus handler.
splitscreenme.detection.description: Which JavaScript files are treated as Nucleus Co-op handlers (and get the checks, suggestions and commands).

enumDescriptions: Handlers open as "Nucleus Co-op handler": JavaScript's colours, with only the handler's suggestions, hovers and checks. VS Code's own JavaScript suggestions (browser globals, newer methods Nucleus' engine doesn't have) stay out.

Handlers stay JavaScript, so VS Code's JavaScript and TypeScript features run on them too (for example "// @ts-check" with Nucleus: Set Up Type Definitions). Their suggestions mix in with the handler's.
splitscreenme.languageMode.markdownDescription: The language mode Nucleus Co-op handlers open in. The language shows in the status bar; click it to switch one file.

splitscreenme.completion.enable.description: Provide completion, hover and signature help for the Nucleus Co-op handler API. Turned off automatically by "Set Up Type Definitions", since TypeScript then provides them.

splitscreenme.showWhatsNew.description: After an update of the Nucleus Co-op handler tools, show a short note with what's new (the full list is in Nucleus: What's New).

splitscreenme.lint.enable.description: Report problems in Nucleus Co-op handlers (ES5-only syntax, unknown options, type mismatches, Hub install pitfalls, …).

splitscreenme.lint.packageChecks.description: Check the files in a Nucleus Co-op handler's folder (<Name>/ next to <Name>.js) as they'd go into the .nc: names Windows can't install, files that overwrite each other, broken INI/JSON, very large files, and files the handler uses (Game.Folder + "\\x") that aren't there.

splitscreenme.lint.compareWithHub.description: For a Nucleus Co-op handler with a Hub.Handler.Id line, compare Game.GUID with the version published on hub.splitscreen.me (guid-changed). Downloads that version once and keeps it in the cache.

splitscreenme.gameFolders.markdownDescription: The game's install folder for each Nucleus Co-op handler (file name → folder), set by hand. **Nucleus: Game Folder: Link…** keeps its links on this PC instead (not in a settings file), and they come first. The handler is then checked against the real files (`ExecutableName`, `BinariesFolder`, the symlink and copy lists…), and those lists suggest the game's files. File names and sizes are read, and the game's .exe and DLLs are analysed on your PC (their import tables and names in them, never run) for hook hints; nothing leaves your PC.

splitscreenme.lint.rules.markdownDescription: Override the severity of individual checks on Nucleus Co-op handlers, e.g. `{ "deprecated": "off", "unknown-member": "error" }`. See the [rule list](https://github.com/Snailedlt/nucleus-devtools#lint-rules).

enumDescriptions: "Double" quotes (also what the Hub install reads Game.GameName and Game.ExecutableName between)
splitscreenme.format.quotes.markdownDescription: Quotes around strings when formatting a Nucleus Co-op handler. A string that contains the chosen quote keeps its own, so no escapes are added.

enumDescriptions: A semicolon at the end of every statement that ends without one
splitscreenme.format.semicolons.markdownDescription: Semicolons when formatting a Nucleus Co-op handler. Either way the program stays exactly the same: the formatter checks that it parses to the same code before changing anything.

splitscreenme.nucleusPath.description: Nucleus Co-op installation folder (contains NucleusCoop.exe and "handlers"). Used by "Install Handler into Nucleus Co-op" and "Test in Nucleus Co-op".

players.description: How many players Nucleus sets up (1-16).

keyboard.description: Who has the keyboard and mouse: a player number, "all" (each player their own) or "none".

stopOnEntry.description: Pause on the first statement instead of running to a breakpoint.

configurationSnippets.label: Nucleus: step through a Nucleus Co-op handler
configurationSnippets.description: Run the handler the way Nucleus does, simulated, and pause at breakpoints

walkthroughs.title: Make a Nucleus Co-op handler
walkthroughs.description: From an empty file to a handler players can download from the Hub: write it, let it check itself, try it, step through it, test it in Nucleus Co-op, share it.

steps.title: Start a handler
steps.description:
Start from the template, with the game's name and its .exe, or from a handler that already works for a similar game (same engine, same launcher).
[New Handler…](command:splitscreenme.newHandler)
[Browse the Hub…](command:splitscreenme.browseHub)
In an empty .js file, typing "handler" offers the whole template too.

steps.title: Let it check itself as you type
steps.description: Problems are underlined as you type: red stops Nucleus Co-op, orange is probably wrong. Hover one for why and what to do; Ctrl+. offers the fix. Hover any option for its docs; suggestions know what exists where.

media.altText: Problems in a handler, each explained, with a fix offered

steps.title: Fix everything that can be fixed
steps.description:
One command applies every safe fix in the handler; what needs your decision stays underlined. It can also run whenever you save.
[Fix All Problems That Can Be Fixed](command:splitscreenme.fixAll)

steps.title: Every option and function, explained
steps.description:
The Docs open beside the editor, offline: every option and function in plain words, with examples. Click a name in a hover or a suggestion to open its page, or search by name or by what you want to do ("window title", "mutex").
[Open the Docs](command:splitscreenme.showDocs)
[Search the Docs…](command:splitscreenme.docsSearch)

media.altText: The Docs panel beside a handler: an option's page with its docs and an example

steps.title: Try it before Nucleus Co-op does
steps.description:
Try It runs Game.Play for each player, the way Nucleus Co-op would, and shows what each one gets: window, launch arguments, files changed. Nothing on your PC is touched. It's in the Run button (▷) above a handler.
[Try It](command:splitscreenme.tryIt)

media.altText: The Try It panel: what each player gets

steps.title: Step through it (F5)
steps.description:
Press F5 in a handler (or Debug in the Run button) to run it the way Nucleus Co-op does, simulated, and pause at breakpoints: see each player's Context, the handler's variables and what it did so far, step back and forth.
[Debug the Handler](command:splitscreenme.debugHandler)

media.altText: The debugger paused in a handler, with its variables and Context

steps.title: Link the game's folder
steps.description:
Point it at where the game is installed and the checks can see the real files: the exe's name, the folders to link or copy, the files to suggest.
[Game Folder: Link…](command:splitscreenme.linkGameFolder)

steps.title: Test it in Nucleus Co-op
steps.description:
One click installs the handler (and its folder) into Nucleus Co-op's handlers folder and starts it with the game selected: pick the players and press Play. Turn on the debug log when asked: if something's off, debug-log.txt says why.
[Test in Nucleus Co-op](command:splitscreenme.testInNucleus)
[Open the Debug Log](command:splitscreenme.openNucleusLog)

steps.title: Share it on the Hub
steps.description:
Package makes the .nc file the Hub takes: the handler and its folder. Upload it at [hub.splitscreen.me](https://hub.splitscreen.me/).
[Package Handler for the Hub](command:splitscreenme.packageHandler)
